title: Rename python.el to deg-python.el to avoid collision with Emacs built-in
description:
The file ~/.emacs.d/python.el shares its name with Emacs's built-in python-mode library (lisp/progmodes/python.el in the Emacs distribution). If ~/.emacs.d is ever added to load-path (done explicitly or by a package), any (require 'python) — including the one implicit in this file's own (use-package python) — resolves to this file instead of the built-in one. That triggers a recursive-load error at worst, or silently loads the wrong file at best.

Evidence it's latent-fragile: this file already calls (provide 'deg-init-python) at the bottom, matching the convention for a renamed module but not the filename. Byte-compile with -L ~/.emacs.d reproduces the recursive-load error today.

Fix:
- Rename ~/.emacs.d/python.el to ~/.emacs.d/deg-python.el (matches the existing provide).
- Update init.el's (load "~/.emacs.d/python") to (load "~/.emacs.d/deg-python").
- Consider the same risk class for javascript.el and clojure.el — they collide with package names too, though they don't (require 'javascript)/(require 'clojure) themselves, so less urgent.
notes: Scope expanded: user requested all three renames (python.el, javascript.el, clojure.el) together rather than deferring the latter two. Same mechanical change for each. clojure.el has no existing (provide ...) form; leaving it that way (not in scope to add one). Header comments in python.el and javascript.el contain the old filename and will be updated to match the new names.
close_reason: Renamed python.el, javascript.el, clojure.el to deg-*.el; init.el load paths updated. Verified file content unchanged apart from header/trailer comments.

title: Remove marketbuzzr venv path from global exec-path
description: init.el:128 bakes /Users/deg/Documents/marketbuzzr/nutshell-mvp/backend/.venv/bin into the global exec-path via custom-set-variables. This almost certainly got saved by Custom UI while working in that project — it now pollutes every Emacs session regardless of which project is open. Remove the specific venv path; rely on poetry-tracking-mode and exec-path-from-shell to inject the correct venv per-project.
notes:
Design decisions:
- Remove the entire (exec-path '(...)) entry from init.el's custom-set-variables, not just the marketbuzzr path. The baked list also contained dead Linux paths (/snap/bin, /usr/lib/emacs/24.5/x86_64-linux-gnu, /usr/games, /usr/local/games) from an old Ubuntu install — cleaning them up in the same pass.
- Restore exec-path-from-shell-initialize at init.el:54-58 (currently commented out). User's zsh $PATH was verified to contain /opt/homebrew/bin, ~/bin, ~/.local/bin, ~/.pyenv/shims plus MacPorts, gcloud, maven, anaconda — strictly richer than the baked list once the unwanted entries are dropped.
- Leave python.el's safety (add-to-list 'exec-path "/opt/homebrew/bin") as-is. It's explicitly a defense against venv activation stripping Homebrew; the comment documents the reason.
- Tradeoff: Emacs's exec-path now depends on shell config correctness. Single source of truth vs baked-in stability. User authorized.

title: Fix flycheck-temp-prefix hardcoded path in javascript.el
description: python.el:152 carefully sets flycheck-temp-prefix to (concat temporary-file-directory "flycheck-deg") — portable across machines. But javascript.el:85 hardcodes /Users/deg/.emacs-flycheck-deg/. Because javascript.el loads after python.el (per init.el), the hardcoded path wins globally, defeating the portability fix. Remove the setq-default line from javascript.el.
notes: Design decision: delete the setq-default line in javascript.el entirely. python.el already sets flycheck-temp-prefix to a portable (concat temporary-file-directory "flycheck-deg") value; no replacement needed in javascript.el. No comment explaining the removal (per no-change-narrative rule).

title: Consolidate multiple custom-set-variables blocks
description: init.el:110 has a custom-set-variables block whose own comment warns 'Your init file should contain only one such instance. If there is more than one, they won't work right.' But bindings.el has three more blocks (lines 48-57, 67-71, 77-78). Custom UI writes can silently clobber values across blocks depending on load order. Fold all bindings.el custom-set-variables content into the single block in init.el, or move them to plain (setq ...) forms if they aren't Custom-managed.
notes:
Design decisions:
- Convert bindings.el's comint custom-set-variables block to setq. Variables have no defcustom setters, so setq is safe. setq in bindings.el (not init.el) keeps inline comments safe from Customize UI rewrites, which would strip them if they lived inside init.el's custom-set-variables block.
- Fix malformed entry: '(comint-prompt-read-only) with no value becomes (setq comint-prompt-read-only t) — matches the inline comment intent ('prompts text is read only').
- Delete magit custom-set-variables block entirely. Every entry is already a verbatim duplicate in init.el's custom block.
- Delete (fill-column 88) block. init.el has (fill-column 100) which is the wanted global default.
- New: text-mode-hook with (setq-local fill-column 88) for prose wrapping. markdown-mode derives from text-mode, so one hook covers both. Caveat: other text-derived modes (html-mode via sgml-mode, message-mode, rst-mode, etc.) will also get 88-col wrap; this is intentional — treat it as 'prose modes get 88.'

title: Add ace-window package to Emacs config
description: Install and configure ace-window package for smarter window management. Replaces C-x o with a letter-based window picker that scales to 3+ windows. Includes dispatch system for swap, delete, maximize, and split operations from a single keybinding (M-o). Add to my-packages in packages.el and configure with use-package.
notes:
Design decisions:
- Bind only C-x o to ace-window (replacing built-in other-window).  User prefers aggressive replacement so muscle memory pushes them toward the richer picker; M-o not bound.
- aw-keys = home-row ('a 's 'd 'f 'g 'h 'j 'k 'l).  Default is 1..9; home-row is the common ergonomic recommendation.
- aw-dispatch-always left at default nil: 2-window layouts are an instant toggle, 3+ windows show the picker overlay.
- Dispatch actions left at ace-window defaults (x delete, m swap, M move, c copy, v split-v, b split-h, o maximize, ? help, etc.).
- use-package block placed in display.el near winner-mode, since it is window-management config.
- Package added to my-packages in packages.el.

title: Magit steals vterm window when opening with C-c g
description:
Problem: When working with both a Magit buffer and a Claude vterm buffer side by side, pressing C-c g (magit-status) sometimes replaces the vterm window instead of appearing in a predictable location. The exact conditions are unclear -- it depends on Emacs window selection heuristics.

Context:
- C-c g is bound to magit-status in bindings.el:33
- vterm buffers (both C-x ! and C-c c Claude vterm) have no special window protection
- There is no display-buffer-alist configuration or dedicated-window setup

Likely fix: Mark vterm windows as dedicated via set-window-dedicated-p in a vterm-mode-hook. This tells Emacs display machinery to never reuse a vterm window for other buffers.

Alternative approaches if dedicated windows prove too restrictive:
- display-buffer-alist rules to prevent magit buffers from landing in vterm windows
- Custom magit-display-buffer-function

Acceptance criteria:
- Opening Magit with C-c g never replaces a visible vterm buffer
- Normal vterm usage (switching buffers manually, etc.) is not impaired
close_reason: Added set-window-dedicated-p hook in display.el to mark vterm windows as dedicated

title: Enable visual-line-mode in Markdown buffers
description: Markdown files often have long prose paragraphs. Without visual-line-mode, lines wrap at the window edge with continuation indicators, and movement commands (C-n/C-p, C-a/C-e) operate on logical lines rather than visual lines — awkward for prose editing. Enable visual-line-mode so wrapping happens at word boundaries and cursor movement follows the visual layout.
notes:
Decisions:
- Scope: markdown-mode only (not all text-derived modes), via a dedicated markdown-mode-hook.
- Enable visual-line-mode for soft-wrap at word boundaries.
- Disable auto-fill-mode defensively (it's not enabled globally today, but if it ever is, markdown should stay opt-out).
- Leave fill-column at 88 (inherited from text-mode-hook). M-q still works as before — user wants to keep manual fill available, just not have hard wraps inserted automatically. Rationale: downstream Markdown renderers handle paragraphs fine without mid-paragraph hard breaks.
close_reason: Added markdown-mode-hook in init.el enabling visual-line-mode and disabling auto-fill-mode. fill-column inherits from text-mode-hook, so M-q still works on demand. Byte-compile clean.

title: Add lexical-binding: t header to all .el files
description:
javascript.el already has ';;; -*- lexical-binding: t; -*-' on its first line. The remaining files in ~/.emacs.d/ all trigger the 'file has no lexical-binding directive on its first line' byte-compile warning: init.el, packages.el, python.el, clojure.el, display.el, bindings.el, bindings-smartparens.el, linux.el, windows.el, deg-tsdh-light-theme.el.

Process: for each file, read it to confirm no dynamic-binding idioms (most commonly: lambdas or let blocks that capture a variable the caller has bound, or defadvice variants that rely on dynamic scope around advised functions). All of these files are short-to-moderate configuration code without closure-building functions, so in practice the conversion is safe — but verify per file before adding the header.

Once verified, prepend the header line:
  ;;; filename.el --- summary  -*- lexical-binding: t; -*-

Byte-compile each to confirm no new warnings appear.

title: Delete irc.el — rcirc/Freenode no longer used
description:
User confirmed they no longer use IRC inside Emacs. irc.el currently:
- Targets irc.freenode.net, which is dead since mid-2021 (community moved to Libera.Chat).
- Uses obsolete APIs: defadvice (obsolete since Emacs 30.1) and defun-rcirc-command (obsolete since Emacs 28.1). Both will error in future Emacs releases.
- Is loaded unconditionally at startup via init.el.

Fix:
- Delete ~/.emacs.d/irc.el.
- Remove the (load "~/.emacs.d/irc") line from init.el.
- Grep the rest of the config for rcirc/irc references and remove any orphans.
- Optional: the comments in the file reference nickserv passwords — confirm nothing sensitive should be preserved before removing from git.

title: Silence byte-compile warnings in javascript.el
description:
Byte-compiling javascript.el produces five warnings:

  file has no 'lexical-binding' directive on its first line
  assignment to free variable 'js2-global-externs'
  the function 'exec-path-from-shell-initialize' is not known to be defined
  the function 'prettier-mode' is not known to be defined
  the function 'company-mode' is not known to be defined

Fixes:
- Add ';;; -*- lexical-binding: t; -*-' header on first line. javascript.el contains no lambdas or dynamic-binding-dependent code, so lexical semantics are safe.
- Add (defvar js2-global-externs) near the existing (defvar flycheck-disabled-checkers) to silence the free-variable warning. The setq is inside a with-eval-after-load 'js2-mode form so js2-mode is loaded before assignment; the defvar is only a compile-time declaration.
- Add (declare-function company-mode "company"), (declare-function prettier-mode "prettier"), (declare-function exec-path-from-shell-initialize "exec-path-from-shell") near the existing flycheck-add-mode declaration.

title: Help/Apropos from vterm pops new frame instead of splitting
description:
Symptom: pressing C-h v (or any help key) while point is in a vterm buffer opens *Help* in a brand-new Emacs frame, rather than splitting the current frame. Same for C-h a (*Apropos*), C-h i (*Info*), and C-h on errors (*Backtrace*).

Root cause: interaction of three existing settings in display.el:

1. (set-window-dedicated-p (selected-window) t) in vterm-mode-hook — vterm windows are dedicated, so display-buffer refuses to put anything else there (intended; prevents Magit etc. from stealing vterm windows).
2. (setq pop-up-windows nil) — global policy that forbids display-buffer from splitting the current frame to make room.
3. (add-to-list 'same-window-buffer-names "*Help*") — obsolete since Emacs 24.3; display-buffer-alist is the modern equivalent and takes precedence.

When display-buffer is asked to show *Help* while point is in a vterm:
  - Try the current (vterm) window → refused by dedication.
  - Try another visible window → none, if only vterm is showing.
  - Try to split the current frame → refused by pop-up-windows nil.
  - Fall back to opening a new frame ← this is the observed behavior.

Fix: add a display-buffer-alist rule for help-like buffers that authorizes display-buffer-pop-up-window (split) explicitly, overriding pop-up-windows nil for just these patterns.

(add-to-list 'display-buffer-alist
             '("\\*\\(Help\\|Apropos\\|[Ii]nfo\\|Backtrace\\)\\*"
               (display-buffer-reuse-window
                display-buffer-pop-up-window
                display-buffer-use-some-window)))

Why it's safe: does not weaken vterm dedication. Magit and other packages still cannot steal vterm windows. Only Help/Apropos/Info/Backtrace get permission to split the current frame, which creates a new non-dedicated window next to the vterm, leaving vterm intact.

title: Remove duplicate global-company-mode and global-flycheck-mode hooks
description: global-company-mode is added to after-init-hook in both init.el:72 and javascript.el:24. global-flycheck-mode is enabled in both python.el:146 (via use-package :init) and javascript.el:32 (add-hook). Harmless but redundant — pick one location (ideally init.el for globals) and remove the others.
notes: Design decision: minimal change. Canonical homes: init.el (global-company-mode via after-init-hook) and python.el (global-flycheck-mode via use-package :init). Delete the duplicate hook declarations in javascript.el along with their now-orphaned section comments. Leave the rjsx-mode-specific company-mode hook at javascript.el:27 alone — redundant with global company, but narrowly scoped and harmless.

title: Remove dead Mac keyboard modifier block in bindings.el
description: bindings.el lines 87-94 have two back-to-back (when (eq system-type 'darwin) ...) forms. Both execute sequentially, so the second silently wins and the first is unreachable dead code. Additionally, init.el:154 sets ns-command-modifier via custom-set-variables — three places configuring the Mac modifier, only one effective. Decide which behavior is wanted (meta vs super on Command), then keep exactly one definition.
notes:
Design decisions:
- Delete entire bindings.el block (both (when (eq system-type 'darwin) ...) forms, both section comments, and the [TODO] about keyboard-toggle command).
- mac-command-modifier / mac-option-modifier only exist in the emacs-mac (Mituharu) port. User runs the standard NS build, where these variables are no-ops regardless of value or load order — all six assignment lines are dead code.
- Live setting stays in init.el's custom-set-variables: '(ns-command-modifier 'meta). ns-option-modifier is unset, so Option keeps native macOS behavior (typing €, ©, etc.).
- [TODO] about auto-detecting keyboards or adding a toggle command is obsolete: macOS has per-connected-keyboard modifier remapping in System Settings → Keyboard → Modifier Keys. No Elisp toggle needed.

title: Strip change-narrative comments from python.el
description:
python.el contains many 'Previously X... changed to Y because Z...' comments added during its evolution — lines 26-33, 37-69, 95-105, 111-125, 154-166, 179-186, 199-208, 216-220, 248-252, 255-275, 277-305 all contain this pattern to some degree.

Per feedback memory feedback_no_change_narrative_comments: change history belongs in git commits, not source. Current behavior is what the comment should describe. When a comment explains 'this used to be X, now it's Y,' only keep the *why the current code does what it does* part (if any), delete the rest.

After this trim, python.el will be substantially shorter and easier to read. Preserve all actual code and any comment that explains a non-obvious WHY of the current implementation.

title: Trim stale TODO list from top of init.el
description:
init.el:1-17 has a [TODO] comment block that predates most of the current config. Items reference Marmalade (removed), worldcognition.com links, prelude, old-style rcirc docs. Many items are either done, obsolete, or no longer applicable:

- 'Disable c-Z behavior' — c-Z is now scroll-up-line in bindings.el (intentional)
- 'Stop crazy window switching' — winner-mode handles this
- 'c-X D should not prompt, unless given arg' — probably fixed in modern dired
- 'Look at everything in https://github.com/bbatsov/prelude' — stale research link
- 'Auto enable auto-fill in .txt and .md files' — related text-mode-hook was added in emacs-nw2 (fill-column); auto-fill-mode is separate but likely not wanted
- 'Get mode where word commands respect camel-case' — subword-mode is in clojure.el (global via prog-mode-hook)
- Windows-related w32-browser items — probably stale

Review each bullet, delete the obsolete ones, and keep only items still actionable. Aim to either clear the section or reduce it to ≤5 current items.

title: Trim Slack transcript from clojure.el
description:
clojure.el contains roughly 200 lines (~22 through ~246) of a pasted Slack conversation about Clojure JVM heap settings (the -Xmx / LEIN_JVM_OPTS discussion with ghadi, noisesmith, dpsutton, adambard). The substantive output of that conversation was preserved as two defun forms at the bottom of the file (jack-in-with-memory, jack-in-clojurescript-with-memory); the transcript itself adds no value to the current code and is recoverable from git if ever needed.

Also trim the heavily-nested commented-out blocks (';;;;;--old 01Aug16 old--;;;;' comment markers, lines ~267 onward — old nrepl/leiningen configuration).

Keep the two defun forms and any live code. After trim the file should be ~50 lines instead of ~350.

title: Wrap over-80-column docstrings in packages.el and python.el
description:
Two docstrings trigger the 'docstring wider than 80 characters' byte-compile warning:

- packages.el:83 — my/claude-vterm docstring (Open or switch to a dedicated vterm buffer running Claude for the current project.)
- python.el:156 — ruff-format-buffer docstring (Format the current Python buffer with ruff, preserving cursor position intelligently.)

Both just need a line break inserted. Emacs convention: the first line should be a complete sentence ≤80 chars, then a blank line, then the rest of the docstring.

title: Silence remaining byte-compile free-variable / free-function warnings
description:
Byte-compiling the full config (emacs --batch -Q -L ~/.emacs.d -f batch-byte-compile *.el) still produces free-variable and 'function is not known to be defined' warnings in several files. Pattern to silence them matches what was done in javascript.el (emacs-vcr):

- Free variable warnings: add (defvar VAR) declarations near the top of the file, where VAR is the symbol being assigned.
- Free function warnings: add (declare-function FUNC "package-name") declarations near the top.

Files with warnings:
- bindings.el — compilation-mode-map, comint-*, magit-mode-map, global-undo-tree-mode
- display.el — recentf-max-menu-items, recentf-list, x11-maximize-frame, x-send-client-message
- init.el — global-auto-revert-non-file-buffers, undo-tree-auto-save-history, exec-path-from-shell-initialize
- packages.el — vterm-shell, vterm-max-scrollback, vterm-mode-map, vterm, magit-last-seen-setup-instructions
- python.el — python-shell-interpreter, python-shell-interpreter-args, python-mode-map, pyvenv-activate, comint-clear-buffer, global-flycheck-mode, projectile-mode, tree-sitter-hl-mode, python-shell-calculate-command
- clojure.el — cider-cljs-lein-repl

Cosmetic-only: runtime behavior is unchanged. Do after emacs-<lexical-binding bead>, since lexical-binding sometimes changes which warnings appear.

title: Replace obsolete term-setup-hook in linux.el with tty-setup-hook
description: linux.el:29 uses term-setup-hook, obsolete since Emacs 24.4. Byte-compile flags it. The documented replacements are tty-setup-hook (for tty-specific setup) and emacs-startup-hook (for anything init-time). The function that hook invokes (remove-escape-from-local-function-key-map) modifies local-function-key-map, which is a tty concern — tty-setup-hook is the correct target.
